candidates.name: Old Town Hall
candidates.price: Free. Although you still have to obtain a ticket!
candidates.content: Built in 1556 in the Renaissance style and remains one of Germany's largest. The position of the tower follows the ancient ideal of "golden mean". Located on the pretty main square of the city, it is a good orientation point. The

candidates.name: St. Thomas Church
candidates.hours: Mon-Thu 10:00 - 18:00; Fri 10:00 - 16:00; Sat 10:00 - 13:30, 16:30 - 18:00; Sun 11:30 - 17:30; churchtower is open weekends only
candidates.content: The church where Johann Sebastian Bach worked as a cantor from 1723 until his death in 1750. His remains are buried under a bronze epitaph near the altar. The Bach Museum is next to the church. Regular concerts are given by the St

candidates.name: Nikolaikirche
candidates.content: Leipzig's largest church. Starting point for the peaceful revolution on October 9, 1989, when 600 Socialist Unity Party members, who were sent to break up the protest, joined the protesters. Every Monday at 17:00 since 1982, the c

candidates.name: Russische Gedächtniskirche
candidates.content: One of the many traces of the Napoleonic wars in and around Leipzig: a memorial church to the honours of Russian soldiers who died during the Napoleonic wars.

candidates.name: Propsteikirche St. Trinitatis
candidates.content: Modern architecture in the style of New Objectivity, covered with a traditional red porphyr stone. Easily to be confused with a modern office building, this church dedicated in 2015 is the largest newly built church building in Ea

candidates.name: Zeitgeschichtliches Forum
candidates.content: Opened in 1999, this is a museum about East Germany (the GDR). There is one permanent exhibition about the life in the GDR and the fall of the GDR; the other exhibition changes about every two months and has similar topics.

candidates.name: Museum in der "Runden Ecke"
candidates.content: Housed in the former headquarters of the GDR secret police, the Stasi, this is an interesting museum documenting the Stasi and its methods of controlling and manipulating the people. Displays are in German; there is not much Engli

candidates.name: Museum der bildenden Künste
candidates.price: Permanent collection: €5 adults; temporary exhibitions: €8; combined ticket: €10; free entry every first Wednesday of the month
candidates.content: Housed in a glass cube, this museum features paintings from the 15th century through today. Highlights include paintings by local artists Max Beckman and Max Klinger, as well as Caspar David Friedrich, Lucas Cranach the Younger, a

candidates.name: Reichsgericht
candidates.price: Admission free; €1 for cloakroom or locker which is refunded
candidates.content: Located across the ring southwest of the New Town Hall (Neues Rathaus), the appearance of this building resembles the original look of the Reichstag in Berlin. It was built from 1888 to 1895 for the Court of the German Empire (Rei

candidates.name: Bach-Museum
candidates.price: €8 adults, €6 concessions; free entry every first Tu of the month
candidates.content: about the composer Johann Sebastian Bach.

candidates.name: Grassi Museum
candidates.content: Includes the Museum of Applied Arts , the Museum of Musical Instruments, and Museum of Ethnology.

candidates.name: Schulmuseum
candidates.content: History of schooling.

candidates.name: Zum Arabischen Coffe Baum
candidates.content: A museum about coffee and coffee culture in Europe's oldest continuously operating coffee house.

candidates.name: Galerie für Zeitgenössische Kunst
candidates.hours: Tue–Fri 14:00-19:00; Sat Sun 12:00-18:00; free entry on Wednesdays
candidates.content: Changing exhibitions of contemporary art.

candidates.name: Naturkundemuseum
candidates.content: The museum of natural history, filled with all kinds of taxidermy creatures.

candidates.name: Sächsisches Psychiatriemuseum
candidates.content: History of psychiatry.

candidates.name: Sächsisches Apothekenmuseum
candidates.content: Pharmacy museum.

candidates.name: Völkerschlachtdenkmal
candidates.alt: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
candidates.price: Adults €12, students & Leipzig Card holders €10, children under 6 free
candidates.content: At 91m tall, this is the biggest monument in Europe, commemorating the Battle of Leipzig in the Napoleonic Wars, in which the combined Prussian, Austrian, and Russian forces defeated Napoleon at a cost of 100,000 lives. The top pl

candidates.name: Leipzig Zoo
candidates.content: This is one of the largest and best known zoos in Germany. In a survey of zoos by Anthony Sheridan, it was ranked first in Germany and second in Europe. The new elephants' enclosure has a swimming pool where you can watch them bat

candidates.name: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek
candidates.price: €5 for day pass (photo ID required); brief glimpse into reading room free
candidates.content: The national library of Germany collects works published in Germany or in the German language. It consists of three buildings from different epochs: the original main building opened in 1916 with two later extensions integrated, a

candidates.name: New Town Hall
candidates.content: Seat of the municipal government since 1905. The building also features a 115-m tower which can be accessed by tour M-F at 14:00.

candidates.name: Torhaus Dölitz
candidates.hours: Wed Fri Sat 10:00–16:00 - subject to change, please call before
candidates.content: Exhibition of pewter figures in historically themed dioramas. The location, the gatehouse and only remainder of an old manor, was one of the hotspots in the battles of the Napoleonic wars.

candidates.name: Mendelssohn House
candidates.price: €7.50 adults, €6 concessions; free entry every second Th of the month; Sunday concert tickets generally are €15/€10
candidates.content: Former home of composer Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy. Regular concerts are held every Sunday at 11:00.

candidates.name: Schiller House
candidates.content: Former home of the poet Friedrich Schiller. This is the (purported) place where he authored the "Ode to Joy".

candidates.name: Schumann House
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 14:00–18:00, Sat Sun 10:00–18:00 (sound space only opened on weekends)
candidates.content: Former house of musicians and composers Clara and Robert Schumann.

candidates.name: Panorama Tower
candidates.hours: Restaurant: Mon–Fri 11:00–00:00, Sat 11:00–01:00, Sun 11:00–23:00; observation platform open from 09:00
candidates.content: Leipzig's highest building has a restaurant and an observation platform at its top with a great view over the town.

candidates.name: Bayerischer Bahnhof
candidates.content: Germany's oldest preserved railway station, built in 1842, only 7 years after the first train line of Germany had been opened. The station is no longer in use but one can still view the portal. In the course of the construction of

candidates.name: Leipzig Riverside Forest
candidates.content: With an area of 2500 hectares (6180 acres), it is one of the largest riparian forests in Central Europe and one of the largest urban forests in Germany. Having an extensive forest—not on the outskirts, but in the middle of the cit

candidates.name: Clara-Zetkin Park
candidates.content: Really a collection of several parks that locals may still know and refer to by their original names: Johannapark, Albertpark, Volkspark Scheibenholz, and Palmengarten. Walk westwards from the new city hall to find the Johannapark

candidates.name: Red Bull Arena
candidates.content: RB Leipzig play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. RB stands for "RasenBallsport and nothing to do with ownership by Red Bull fizzy drinks" but some fans doubt this assertion. With a capacity of 48,000 for Bundesliga games and 42

candidates.name: Oper Leipzig
candidates.content: The opera house of Leipzig. Though the building was opened in 1960, the company looks back at more than 300 years of history.

candidates.name: Bach Festival
candidates.content: Organized by the Bach Museum.

candidates.name: Leipziger Buchmesse
candidates.content: Besides the main event on the fairground, readings take place in various locations around the city.

candidates.name: Leipziger Kleinmesse
candidates.content: Funfair, twice a year in spring (April/May) and fall (September/October).

candidates.name: Euro-Scene
candidates.content: Festival of contemporary European theatre.

candidates.name: Sightseeing tour
candidates.content: The tour lasts 2½ hours, comprising a 1-hour guided walk through the city centre and a bus tour of 1½ hours to sights elsewhere. You can also book each part of the tour individually. Buy your ticket at tourist information, where t

candidates.name: Sightseeing by tram
candidates.hours: Saturdays, starting at 11:00 and 14:00; May–September also Sundays 11:00
candidates.content: Every weekend, LVB offers sightseeing tours in a modified tram called "Gläserner Leipziger". Buy your ticket in advance from any of the LVB service offices listed above; it includes a day ticket for zone 110 (Leipzig) of the MDV n

candidates.name: videoSightseeing Leipzig
candidates.hours: individual starting time for small groups
candidates.content: In addition to the comments of a live guide in English or other languages, on-screen historic film footage and photographs give you a deeper insight into Leipzig's history and life today. The standard length of the tour is 2 hours

candidates.name: Motets in St. Thomas Church
candidates.hours: Fri 18:00 and Sat 15:00; unreserved seating, come early (church opens 45 min before)
candidates.content: Listen to the St. Thomas Boys Choir performing Bach's music in its original environment. Be aware that a guest choir may sing instead at any time as the St Thomas Choir travels a lot. Since the motet is primarily a musical form of

candidates.name: Rosental
candidates.content: The second largest park of Leipzig is northwest of the city centre. From the Rosental you can get a glimpse into the zoo without having to pay the entrance fee (Zooschaufenster near the large meadow). Crossing Waldstraße and conti

candidates.name: Wildpark
candidates.content: Watch wild animals in the woods. If you feel like hiking, after passing through the Wildpark you can turn northwards and walk to Clara-Zetkin Park, or walk south/southeast to Cospudener See. Both are about 2.5 km away.

candidates.name: Bootsverleih Herold
candidates.price: €7.50/hr for two-seaters; motorboat tour (70 min incl. drink) €14
candidates.content: Boat rental offering skiffs (up to 4 persons), kayaks (for 1, 2 or 2+child) and Canadian canoes (for 2, 3, 4 or 5 persons); as well as guided motorboat tours (advance booking required).

candidates.name: Bootsverleih am Klingerweg
candidates.price: €8/hr for two-seaters; motorboat tour (70 min incl. coffee) €14
candidates.content: Boat rental offering skiffs (up to 4 persons), kayaks (for 1, 2 or 2+child) and Canadian canoes (for 3 or 4), large Canadian for 10 (requires a professional cox, advance booking); guided motorboat tours.

candidates.name: BMW Werk Leipzig
candidates.price: €6 per person (adult), €130 for an individual tour (for up to 30 persons)
candidates.content: The BMW assembly plant in Leipzig, which builds the 1er-series and X1 models, offers guided tours of its premises. They require previous appointment - you need to send a request with your preferences in advance and wait for the Vi

candidates.name: Porsche Leipzig
candidates.content: The Porsche factory in Leipzig, which builds the Cayenne and the Panamera, offers plant tours as well as driving experiences on the test track, combined with meals at the on-site restaurant. A much wider choice of events is offere

candidates.name: Gewandhaus
candidates.content: Mendelssohn's orchestra still exists, but the concert hall is new. Inside is a huge painting by Sighard Gille, visible through the windows from Augustusplatz.

candidates.name: Wave-Gotik-Treffen Leipzig
candidates.hours: Date follows Pentecost, late May or early June
candidates.content: World's largest goth festival includes a pagan village, medieval market, and goth music.

candidates.name: Auerbachs Keller
candidates.content: This pub has been around since medieval times. Opened in 1525, it is among the oldest continuously operated pubs in Germany. The barrel cellar (only opened for private parties) has been the background to a scene in one of Germany'

candidates.name: Gosenschenke Ohne Bedenken
candidates.content: Includes the city's prettiest beer garden but not many vegetarian options. Try their beer specialty 'Gose'. It's made with coriander and salt, and is very much an acquired taste. It is usually served with a shot of liquor.

candidates.name: Bayerischer Bahnhof Gasthaus & Gosebrauerei
candidates.content: Brewery and restaurant in the former ticket hall of Leipzig's oldest railway station.

candidates.name: Tonelli's
candidates.content: Right in the centre of town. Good German food and drink at a low price. A local mainstay. The only location that offers live music Monday to Saturday starting at 21:00. Tuesdays is "Guitarnight" with guitar guru Christian Rover an

candidates.name: Moritzbastei & Cafe Barbakane
candidates.content: Very old and big student club bar and cafe. Underground cellars. Live bands or DJs most nights, outdoor films are shown in the summer. Moritzbastei was once a part of the city wall. Students dug it out in the 1970s and turned it i

candidates.name: Chocolate
candidates.content: Sleek design.

candidates.name: Sixtina
candidates.content: Has the largest number of different brands of absinthe.

candidates.name: Volkshaus
candidates.content: Always a happening place. DJs, football games, and partying all night.

candidates.name: Spizz
candidates.content: Right in the centre of town. Popular with all age groups. A place to see and be seen. Also a jazz bar with brass instruments hanging from the ceiling.

candidates.name: Conne Island
candidates.content: Former squat house, now a top venue for punk, rock, ska, and hip-hop concerts.

candidates.name: Dark Flower
candidates.content: gothic music and dark wave, on Thursday rock music.

candidates.name: Elipamanoke
candidates.content: Dark and dirty techno club with two floors in an old industrial building in the Plagwitz district.

candidates.name: Flowerpower
candidates.content: Weirdly decorated place with hippie 1970s theme. Mostly classic rock. Party lasts well past 04:00.

candidates.name: Zills Tunnel
candidates.content: Saxon food. Large portions. Outdoor terrace, rustic cellar, or tunnel courtyard.

candidates.name: Zest
candidates.content: Vegetarian/vegan restaurant. Try the strawberry basil smoothie.

candidates.name: Barthel's Hof
candidates.content: Exotic Saxon dishes.

candidates.name: Medici
candidates.content: Classy Italian restaurant

candidates.name: Stadtpfeiffer
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat from 18:00; closed in July and August

candidates.name: Wurstmeister
candidates.content: A Snackbar with German food

candidates.name: Gaststätte Kollektiv
candidates.content: A nostalgic German restaurant

candidates.name: Olive Tree
candidates.content: A kebab restaurant.

candidates.name: Christmas Market
candidates.content: As in many other German cities, Leipzig hosts the Leipziger Weinachtsmarkt, or Leipzig Christmas Market, which opens in the last week of November, first week of December and continues until a few days before Christmas Day. The Lei

candidates.name: Hauptbahnhof
candidates.content: The Hauptbahnhof is not only one of the biggest train stations in Europe, it's a great shopping mall as well (on three floors boutiques and restaurants are located next to drug stores and supermarkets)

candidates.name: Fresh Food Market
candidates.content: may be a bit cheaper (mostly lower-grade goods at a lower price and some discount offers) but the atmosphere is not so nice. Sometimes there are market criers around.

candidates.name: Westpaket
candidates.content: A nice alternative fleamarket with approx. 100 booths of locals selling handmade stuff, some antiques and second hand clothes on the pavements. there are also some music groups and food.
